method.allAssets: All 130 persisted JPEGs visually inspected through 25 contact sheets. Contact inspection covers composition and obvious state/layout problems; it is not full-resolution text acceptance.
method.originalInspection: 22 selected original JPEGs opened separately at original resolution for concrete findings, destructive confirmations, reviews, mobile states, unavailable/empty states and one representative per area.
method.identity: All 130 decoded assets verified against Git blob SHA1 and tree byte size; originals kept unchanged.
method.runtime: No app run, clicks, tests or CI. Stills do not establish keyboard behavior, scroll operability, auth, API success or post-save behavior.
method.provenance: These are existing persisted screenshots on dev; sourceRun/sourceProduct in each asset is preserved. They are not fresh captures of baseline dev and contain synthetic design test data.

findings.title: Talent review displays internal leader UUID
findings.observation: The Leader/Líder input exposes d739750b-960e-4669-86a5-fdb233c97263 instead of the person's display name. The same source identifier is visible in contact-level detail and review captures.
findings.impact: The user cannot confidently identify the manager from the editable record.
findings.suggestion: Resolve leader ID to a human-readable name in form, detail and review while preserving the ID only internally.

findings.title: Portuguese forms still expose English/raw status values
findings.observation: The pt-BR Talent editor shows Perspectiva=Grow. The pt-BR quarterly performance editor shows Status do 1º/2º trimestre=on and Status do 3º trimestre=ahead.
findings.impact: Mixed language and raw enum values make the business workflow feel unfinished.
findings.suggestion: Provide localized display labels for enumerated values in forms and review summaries without changing their stored codes.

findings.title: Destructive final actions use the standard blue primary style
findings.observation: Delete incident and Delete record are blue primary buttons. Team Structure's Delete leader uses a muted red-text destructive action; operations detail/list delete actions also use red text.
findings.impact: The final destructive action loses the visual warning used in adjacent flows.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same danger treatment to final destructive confirmations and keep cancellation visually secondary.

findings.title: Risk deletion preview says the record is already unavailable
findings.observation: The proposed values card reads 'This record is no longer available' while the final button is still Delete record. The incident equivalent says 'This record will be deleted' and includes 'This action cannot be undone.'
findings.impact: The risk review can be read as a retrieval error rather than a pending deletion.
findings.suggestion: Use future-tense deletion language with the record name and explicit consequence in the proposal/effects block.

findings.title: Gallery uses the technical HuGR shell
findings.observation: Desktop captures display HuGR, DEV, a 127.0.0.1 origin in the eyebrow, Context and access, Choose a project and Build what matters. With agents. They do not show a Teams profile or Sucafina-branded host.
findings.impact: Domain-level polish alone cannot demonstrate the intended Sucafina/Teams product experience.
findings.suggestion: Qualify the intended host/brand/profile composition separately and recapture the actual user entry path.
findings.caveat: This is evidence of the captured composition, not proof that Teams profile or Sucafina branding is absent from the code.

findings.title: Mobile tables hide columns beyond the captured viewport
findings.observation: At 320px the Headcount Leaders header ends at 'Ta…' and the Projects list shows only Project/Status in the frame. No horizontal-scroll affordance is visible in these captures. Review action stacks remain entirely visible in separate captures.
findings.impact: Discoverability of off-screen columns/actions needs a focused interaction check.
findings.suggestion: Verify horizontal scrolling and provide an obvious cue or a responsive card representation for essential row information.
findings.caveat: A still image cannot establish that the columns or actions are inaccessible. This is not logged as a proven overflow/scroll bug.

findings.title: Portuguese forms display US-style dates
findings.observation: pt-BR editor captures show 02/14/2022 for the member start date and 11/28/2026 for the campaign end date.
findings.impact: Ambiguous day/month interpretation remains possible in a Portuguese flow.
findings.suggestion: Verify browser/input locale behavior and ensure the intended user's date format is consistent.
findings.caveat: These native date-input formats may depend on the capture browser locale; the screenshot establishes the presentation, not the responsible code path.

method.selection: 30 JPEGs selected from the latest canonical galleries at the fixed candidate SHA: principal+representative detail/review for each available area, plus recorded UI42/UI44 failures. Historical 477 JPEGs were not all reviewed.
method.contact: All 30 selected originals triaged on five contact sheets.
method.fullOriginal: 18 selected originals separately opened and inspected, including every area with available images.
method.identity: All 30 verified against Git blob SHA1 and byte size. Originals unchanged.
method.runtime: No app run, interaction, new tests or CI. Qualification claims from gallery documents are attributed source claims, not new runtime verification or human design acceptance.

findings.kind: qualification/evidence gap, not inferred runtime cause
findings.title: Scenario and sensitivity result journeys are incomplete in the latest preserved attempt
findings.observation: UI42 failure image shows Preview combinations Running, disabled inputs, a preview-unavailable skeleton and no history. UI44 failure image shows Lost connection to the server/Retrying, retained review and disabled confirmation. Attempt19 explicitly says UI43 results were not reached; no UI43 JPEG exists in the inventoried477 candidate images.
findings.implication: These areas cannot be called completed or visually accepted on result states from this evidence.
findings.caveat: Backend completion after the failed browser wait remains unknown. This audit did not rerun the operations.

findings.title: Technical IDs and field paths dominate primary business content
findings.observation: Constraints show a UUID; sensitivity review shows decision-result/parameter IDs and raw lte; preserved review fields use opexOwners[id:...].budget and .id; mobile comparison repeats full source lineage; relationships show UUID→sf-source; discussion author is macos:...:1001; confirmation shows a long confirmation-selection identifier; import changes show /versions/@id=.../lines/@id=.../f/0 before the values.
findings.implication: The source identity is preserved but the operator must decode internal schema to understand the record and change.
findings.suggestion: Resolve user-facing names and field labels; lead with human-readable entity/change summaries and keep exact references in an expandable provenance section or copy action. Do not invent absent source labels.

findings.title: Exact tiny day values and repeated period labels make the chart hard to scan
findings.observation: The desktop chart shows three Jan1–Dec31 rows with 0.00149947 days and nearly zero-length marks; the mobile table retains a full 0,00163916 value. The visible distinction between rows is chiefly source-reference identity in the table.
findings.implication: Precision is preserved, but the meaning of the comparison is hard to see quickly.
findings.suggestion: Retain exact values in details while giving each row a business label and a clearly explained readable duration. Any conversion must remain derived from the stated source unit.
findings.caveat: Numbers differ across capture moments; this audit does not assert a data mismatch. Source-supplied Portuguese measure labels remain visible inside English chrome.

findings.title: Unavailable source states explain the boundary but offer little navigation
findings.observation: Report entry requires a preserved review reference and states that no native list is published; the main action is disabled. Follow-up proposal displays no current producer review twice, in review and receipt sections, without a next-step control in the viewed frame.
findings.implication: The operator understands why the action is absent but may not know how to obtain the required source/choice.
findings.suggestion: Where authorized routes exist, provide a link to the source selection or preserved review; otherwise explain the next responsible action without fabricating list data or receipts.

findings.title: Stale-source condition appears as a plain sentence below a long value panel
findings.observation: The captured original stale-update state ends with 'The original sources changed or could not be revalidated. Read them again.' beneath the source card. It is visually less prominent than the data above and no direct reread control is visible in that frame.
findings.implication: A user may miss the need to refresh before relying on preserved values.
findings.suggestion: Present the stale condition near the review heading as a clear alert with a visible refresh/read action, while retaining source provenance.
findings.caveat: This is a static hierarchy observation; focus and announcement behavior were not tested.

findings.title: Candidate screenshots continue to use the technical HuGR shell
findings.observation: Desktop screenshots show HuGR, local origin, Context and access and project selection. None of the selected candidate images demonstrates the Teams profile entry path.
findings.implication: These captures support domain-screen assessment, not acceptance of the final Sucafina/Teams host.
findings.caveat: Does not prove Teams/profile code is absent.
